summary: DevFolio should be a static site: Astro built ahead of time, no application server, no database, on Cloudflare Pages (the global edge). The pages are read-heavy and the budget is 0 USD a month.

frontend.justification: DevFolio is a content site on web. Twelve month target 3,000 users, peak 50, MVP 2 weeks, 1 beginner engineer. Pre-renders Markdown and pages to static HTML, with small islands of JavaScript only where a page needs them. seo_critical is true, so the public URL has to return real HTML. Team languages: javascript, html, css. The copy is Markdown, which Astro can render at build time.

alternatives.why_not: htmx with server templates is a looser fit for this team and for this kind of product.
Eleventy is a looser fit for this team and for this kind of product.

tradeoffs: A highly interactive app fights the model. Islands get awkward past a simple site.

backend.justification: No accounts, no writes, no private files, and no payments. A server would be a process to patch in exchange for nothing the page needs.

alternatives.why_not: There is no write path, account system, or private data, so a server would only add a bill and a process to patch.

tradeoffs: Any future account or form handler means adding a server later.

database.justification: The pages are generated from files in git. There is no row to store, so there is no database.

alternatives.why_not: There is no dynamic data to store. Markdown in git is the source of truth.

tradeoffs: A form or an account later means adding a database.

hosting.justification: cloud_preference is any, deployment_model is managed_cloud, data_residency resolves to none. The pin is the global edge. Free static hosting with a global CDN and HTTPS. Right when the site has no user data. team.has_devops is false, so a host with a small control surface beats a cluster. There is no process to keep up. Static hosting is the whole platform.

alternatives.why_not: GitHub Pages does not match a 12 month target of 3,000 users and a peak of 50.
Netlify is a worse fit for a monthly infra budget of 0 USD.

tradeoffs: Not a database region. Do not put personal data or a payment record here and call it compliant.

assumptions: Compute (cloudflare_pages, tiny band) about 0 to 0 USD.
Scale band is tiny: 3000 users at 12 months, peak 50, 1.0 GB stored.
This is an order-of-magnitude band, not an invoice. Taxes, support plans, and human time are excluded.

warnings.message: The estimate is zero because the choice stays on a free static tier. A custom domain registrar, if you buy one, is outside this band. A traffic spike past the host's fairness limit is the thing to watch.

assumptions: budget.existing_licences defaulted to an empty list.
data.sensitivity defaulted to public for a content site with no auth.
requirements.expected_rps_peak was not set. Capacity uses peak concurrency (50), which is roughly 5 requests per second if about one in ten connected users acts at once.
